intro.author: Paul, joined by 'all the brethren which are with me' (1:1-2)
intro.written: Debated: possibly about AD 48–49, which would make it one of Paul's earliest letters, or in the early-to-mid 50s
intro.audience: The churches of Galatia in central Asia Minor (modern Turkey), mostly Gentile believers
intro.setting: Paul had founded these churches, but after he left, other teachers arrived insisting that Gentile believers must be circumcised and keep the Law of Moses to belong fully to God's people. Scholars debate whether the churches were the southern cities Paul visited in Acts 13–14 (such as Iconium, Lystra and Derbe) or communities further north. Either way, Paul writes with alarm and urgency.
intro.purpose: Paul defends the gospel of grace and his own calling, and warns the Galatians not to accept circumcision and the Law as requirements for belonging to Christ.
intro.bigIdea: People are made right with God through faith in Christ, not by keeping the Law, and are set free to live by the Spirit.

outline.title: Freedom and life in the Spirit

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE GALATIANS
